title: Kimchi Fried Rice with Fried Egg and Sesame
summary: Day-old rice fried with ripe kimchi, onion, butter and Korean chilli flakes until crisp on the base, then topped with a fully set fried egg, sesame seeds and seaweed. Tangy, spicy and savoury, it is a fast and filling bowl.
equipment: large nonstick frying pan or wok (30 cm)
nonstick frying pan with a lid (24-26 cm)

ingredients.item: cold cooked short- or medium-grain rice (from about 250 g raw), cooked the day before
ripe cabbage kimchi, chopped, plus 60 ml of its juice (check the label: no added alcohol)
ingredients.note: check the label: most shop kimchi contains fish sauce and salted shrimp; use vegan kimchi for a fish- and shellfish-free version

ingredients.item: spring onions, whites and greens sliced separately
sheet unseasoned roasted seaweed (nori), cut into thin strips

steps.title: Separate the rice
steps.text: Break the cold rice into separate grains with your hands, rubbing out any clumps. Chilled, day-old rice has dried out slightly on the surface, so the grains fry and crisp rather than turning sticky.

steps.title: Cook the kimchi
steps.text: Heat the 2 tbsp oil in the large pan over medium-high heat and cook the onion and spring onion whites for 4-5 minutes until soft and lightly browned. Add the kimchi, its juice, the butter and the chilli flakes and cook for 4-6 minutes, stirring, until the kimchi is soft and most of the liquid has gone. Cooking off the juice concentrates its sour, savoury flavour and stops the rice going soggy.

steps.title: Fry the rice
steps.text: Add the rice, turn the heat to medium, and stir and fold for 3 minutes until every grain is coloured, then add the soy sauce and sesame oil. Spread the rice out, raise the heat to medium-high and leave it for 3-4 minutes, stirring only once or twice, until it sticks and crisps on the base and is piping hot all the way through (74°C). Leaving it undisturbed lets a crunchy, toasty crust form. Keep it warm on very low heat.

steps.title: Fry the eggs
steps.text: Heat the 1 tbsp oil in the second pan over medium heat and crack in the eggs. After 2 minutes, cover and cook for 3-4 minutes more until both whites and yolks are completely set (71°C). The lid traps steam, which cooks the top of the eggs through without burning the base.

steps.title: Assemble the bowls
steps.text: Divide the rice among 4 bowls and top each with an egg. Scatter over the spring onion greens, sesame seeds and seaweed strips. The fresh greens and nori add a clean, crisp contrast to the rich, tangy rice.

tips: A common mistake is using freshly cooked rice, which turns gluey; use rice cooked the day before and chilled.
The riper and more sour the kimchi, the better the flavour, so this is a great use for an older jar.
Resist stirring constantly once the rice is spread out, or it will never form a crisp base.
Check the kimchi and soy sauce labels to make sure there is no added alcohol.
storage: Cool quickly, refrigerate within 1 hour and use within 24 hours. Reheat once only until piping hot (74°C), and cook fresh eggs to serve rather than reheating them. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
